requirements.section: 3. Static and Strong Typing (operator precedence and concatenation)
requirements.summary: The `..` operator concatenates: both operands render via toString, the result is always String (`1 .. "x"` is `"1x"`, `"x" .. null` is `"xnull"`), it binds looser than arithmetic, and it is left-associative.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 4 states verbatim: `..` concatenates, both operands render via toString, result always String, `1 .. "x"` is `"1x"`; `a + b .. c` is `(a + b) .. c`. Oracles derived from this text, not captured from the IUT. SOL-TCK-0023 adds the literal `"x" .. null` case quoted verbatim in section 3 and a three-operand chain, where left-associativity makes `1 .. 2 .. 3` equal `(1 .. 2) .. 3` = `123`.
normativeQuotes: Concatenation binds looser than arithmetic, so a + b .. c is (a + b) .. c, and it is left-associative.

requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 3 pairing rule + section 21.9 Required diagnostics table names SEM_EQUALS_WITHOUT_HASHCODE = SOLV-SEM-045. Diagnostic is specification-required, therefore a normative expectation.

requirements.summary: The predeclared `exit(code: Integer)` terminates the program with `code` as the process exit status and runs no further code; an explicit exit(n) is a normal language completion, not a runtime error.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 5 states exit(code) terminates with `code` as process exit status and runs no further code. Section 7/8 classify an explicit exit(n) as a normal completion with a declared language exit status.
normativeQuotes: The predeclared exit(code: Integer) function runs no further Solvik code: it terminates the program with code as the process exit status

requirements.section: 4. Root Type Hierarchy (checked integral arithmetic) / 3 (division by zero)
requirements.summary: Integral arithmetic overflow raises a Solvik runtime arithmetic error; division by zero raises a Solvik runtime arithmetic error.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 4 states verbatim: 'Integral division truncates toward zero and division by zero raises a Solvik runtime arithmetic error' and 'Integral arithmetic is checked and raises a Solvik runtime arithmetic error on overflow'. The expected structured fault is the protocol's normative runtime-error classification of a Solvik arithmetic error (protocol.md section 4.1: ARITHMETIC_ERROR), a spec+protocol derivation, not a value captured from the IUT. Operands are held in `var` bindings so the fault is a genuine run-time event rather than constant folding; oracles authored from the quoted text, with the IUT run only to detect a discrepancy.
normativeQuotes: Integral arithmetic is checked and raises a Solvik runtime arithmetic error on overflow.
Integral division truncates toward zero and division by zero raises a Solvik runtime arithmetic error.

requirements.summary: The `throw` operand type must be assignable to a guest exception type; throwing any other value is the compile-time error SEM_THROW_NON_EXCEPTION (SOLV-SEM-053), reported on the operand.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 22.2 states verbatim: 'The operand type must be assignable to a guest exception type (an exception type per section 22.1); throwing any other value is the compile-time error SOLV-SEM-053 (SEM_THROW_NON_EXCEPTION), reported on the operand.' Section 22.1 defines a guest exception type as a class whose superclass chain reaches Exception, RuntimeException, or ApplicationException. The code appears in section 22.2 and in the section 22.6 required-diagnostic table, so it is specification-required rather than merely implementation-stable (TCK.md section 6). Oracle authored from the quoted text; the IUT was run only to detect a discrepancy.
normativeQuotes: throwing any other value is the compile-time error SOLV-SEM-053 (SEM_THROW_NON_EXCEPTION), reported on the operand.

requirements.summary: A `try` with neither a `catch` clause nor a `finally` clause is the compile-time error SEM_TRY_NEEDS_HANDLER (SOLV-SEM-056), reported on the whole statement.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 22.3 states verbatim: 'A `try` with neither a `catch` clause nor a `finally` clause is the compile-time error SOLV-SEM-056 (SEM_TRY_NEEDS_HANDLER), reported on the whole statement.' The same section's permissive grammar means `try`+`finally` and `try`+`catch` are both legal, so the tested trigger omits BOTH clauses; an earlier draft of this test used `try`+`finally` and was rejected as an invalid oracle before any test ran. Code also listed in section 22.6, so specification-required (TCK.md section 6).
normativeQuotes: A try with neither a catch clause nor a finally clause is the compile-time error SOLV-SEM-056 (SEM_TRY_NEEDS_HANDLER), reported on the whole statement.

requirements.summary: A static member is not inherited and not overridable; declaring `open` or `override` on a static member is the compile-time error SEM_INVALID_STATIC_MODIFIER (SOLV-SEM-047).
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 7 (Static members) states verbatim: 'A static member is **not inherited** and is **not overridable**. ... Declaring `open` or `override` on a static member is `SOLV-SEM-047`.' The static diagnostic table names SEM_INVALID_STATIC_MODIFIER = SOLV-SEM-047 for 'a static member declared `open` or `override`'. Specification-required code (TCK.md section 6). `static open func` is the grammatically valid spelling (grammar: staticMember: STATIC methodDecl; methodModifier: OPEN | OVERRIDE), so the program is well-formed apart from the single named violation.
normativeQuotes: Declaring open or override on a static member is SOLV-SEM-047.
SEM_INVALID_STATIC_MODIFIER | SOLV-SEM-047 | a static member declared open or override

requirements.summary: An expression-position `if` must have an `else`; a missing `else` is the dedicated compile-time error SEM_IF_EXPRESSION_MISSING_ELSE (SOLV-SEM-042) and does not also fabricate a branch-type mismatch.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 21.4 states verbatim: 'An expression `if` must have an `else`; a missing `else` is a dedicated compile-time error and does not also fabricate a branch-type mismatch.' Section 21.9's required-diagnostic table names that dedicated code: SEM_IF_EXPRESSION_MISSING_ELSE = SOLV-SEM-042, primary span 'whole `if` expression'. The 'does not also fabricate a branch-type mismatch' clause is part of the oracle, which is why SOLV-SEM-042 and not SOLV-TYPE-038 is expected. Section 21.4 also states statement-style `if` remains valid without `else`, so the trigger is `if` in expression position.
normativeQuotes: An expression if must have an else; a missing else is a dedicated compile-time error and does not also fabricate a branch-type
SEM_IF_EXPRESSION_MISSING_ELSE | SOLV-SEM-042 | whole if expression

requirements.summary: A `switch` expression must have a default arm; a missing default is the compile-time error SEM_SWITCH_EXPRESSION_MISSING_DEFAULT (SOLV-SEM-043), reported on the whole `switch` expression.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 21.9 lists SEM_SWITCH_EXPRESSION_MISSING_DEFAULT = SOLV-SEM-043, primary span 'whole `switch` expression'. Section 21.9 also states 'existing type errors inside a tail expression keep their existing codes', and SOLV-TYPE-038 is reserved for normally completing branches with no single nearest common declared supertype, so a default-less `switch` expression must be SOLV-SEM-043 rather than a fabricated branch mismatch. Span/location is not asserted: TCK.md section 6.1 forbids choosing an observable the specification leaves undefined.
normativeQuotes: SEM_SWITCH_EXPRESSION_MISSING_DEFAULT | SOLV-SEM-043 | whole switch expression

requirements.summary: A `Result`-typed value used as a standalone statement is the compile-time error SEM_UNUSED_RESULT (SOLV-SEM-052); `compute()` alone is rejected while `compute().ignore()` is accepted.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 23.2 states verbatim: 'A `Result`-typed value used as a standalone statement (a call expression whose result type is a `Result`) is the compile-time error `SEM_UNUSED_RESULT` (`SOLV-SEM-052`)' and 'A standalone `Result` call such as `compute()` therefore requires one of these consumptions; `compute().ignore()` is accepted and `compute()` alone is rejected.' Code named verbatim in the normative text, so specification-required (TCK.md section 6). The `Result` enum declaration follows section 12's structurally recognized two-parameter shape.
normativeQuotes: A Result-typed value used as a standalone statement (a call expression whose result type is a Result) is the compile-time
compute().ignore() is accepted and compute() alone is rejected.

requirements.summary: `unwrap` on an `Err` and `unwrapErr` on an `Ok` raise a Solvik runtime fault of the same class as an arithmetic, cast, or bounds fault: an ordinary guest failure with a non-zero exit status, not an internal error, detected at run time at the operation.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 23's operation table gives the fault condition ('`unwrap` ... faults on the error variant'; '`unwrapErr` ... faults on the success variant'), and section 23.1 states verbatim that these 'raise a Solvik runtime fault of the same class as an arithmetic, cast, or bounds fault (an ordinary guest failure reported to the host with a non-zero exit status, not an internal error)' and 'can only occur on a receiver whose static type is a `Result`, so it is detected at run time (at the operation)'. Run-time detection is why the outcome is RUNTIME_ERROR rather than COMPILE_ERROR. The expected category is the protocol's normative RESULT_WRONG_VARIANT classification (protocol.md section 4.1), a spec+protocol derivation. Source location is NOT asserted even though section 23.1 mentions it, because the spec does not define the exact span and TCK.md section 6.1 forbids the TCK choosing an undetermined observable.
normativeQuotes: unwrap on an Err, unwrapErr on an Ok, and expect on an Err raise a Solvik runtime fault of the same class as an arithmetic, cast,
so it is detected at run time (at the operation)

requirements.summary: A thrown value that reaches the program boundary with no remaining handler is uncaught: a guest-visible failure terminating the program with a non-zero exit status, reported as an ordinary guest error and never as a host internal error.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 22.5 states verbatim: 'When a thrown value reaches this boundary, no Solvik handler remains, so the value is uncaught. An uncaught thrown value is a guest-visible failure: it terminates the program with a non-zero exit status ... and it is reported as an ordinary guest error, never as a host internal error.' Section 22.4 supplies the crossing used by the test ('A `throw` inside a called function is caught by a handler in any dynamically enclosing function frame'), and this program has no handler at any level. Category is the protocol's normative UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION classification (protocol.md section 4.1). The class-and-message report text in section 22.5 is NOT asserted: the spec does not place it on guest stdout, so asserting it would let the TCK choose an undetermined observable (section 6.1).
normativeQuotes: An uncaught thrown value is a guest-visible failure: it terminates the program with a non-zero exit status
and it is reported as an ordinary guest error, never as a host internal

requirements.summary: A `val` binding cannot be reassigned; reassigning an immutable binding is a compile-time error, while mutating a `var` property of an object held in a `val` remains legal.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 2 states 'Reassignment is illegal' with the example `count = 2 // compile error`, and its `val freezes the binding, not the complete reachable object graph` example marks `user.name = "Douglas"` valid and `user = User("Other")` a compile error. IMPORTANT: the specification names NO stable diagnostic code for this rule, so no code is asserted and `diagnosticNormative` is false -- TCK.md section 6 forbids promoting an implementation enum entry to normative status. The manifest therefore asserts only the diagnostic family, which is the protocol's own closed taxonomy (protocol.md section 4.1), and the compile-time category is a section 3 fact ('Assignments are statements, not value-producing expressions' plus the static-typing model).
normativeQuotes: Reassignment is illegal
val freezes the binding, not the complete reachable object graph.

requirements.summary: `val` freezes the binding, not the complete reachable object graph: reassigning a `var` property of an object held in a `val` is legal and the new value is observed by later reads.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 2 states verbatim: '`val` freezes the binding, not the complete reachable object graph', demonstrated by the example where `user.name = "Douglas"` is annotated 'valid' and `user = User("Other")` 'compile error'. This requirement covers the VALID half (property mutation through a `val`); REQ-0300 covers the rejected half (rebinding). Expected stdout is the reassigned name; section 5 states `print` appends no line separator, so the bytes are exactly `Douglas`. No code is involved: this is an acceptance, so the oracle is a plain observable.
normativeQuotes: val freezes the binding, not the complete reachable object graph.
user.name = "Douglas" // valid
user = User("Other")  // compile error

requirements.summary: A raw string is `r` + N '#' + '"' + content + '"' + exactly N '#'; its semantic value is the content between the delimiters, backslash escapes are not processed, and embedded newlines are preserved.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 15 gives the rule verbatim: 'r + N \'#\' characters + \'"\' + content + \'"\' + exactly N \'#\' characters', states 'The token\'s semantic value is the content between the delimiters', and lists that raw strings 'do not process backslash escapes' and 'preserve embedded newlines'. From this: (a) an N=1 raw string keeps its backslash literally, so the JSON text reproduces byte-for-byte; (b) inside r###"..."### an embedded `"#` is a quote followed by ONE hash, not exactly three, so it does not close the token and is part of the value; (c) the newline immediately after the opening delimiter and before the closing delimiter is content. Every expected byte is determined by the quoted rule, not by the IUT.
normativeQuotes: r + N '#' characters + '"' + content + '"' + exactly N '#' characters
The token's semantic value is the content between the delimiters.
do not process backslash escapes
preserve embedded newlines

requirements.summary: Normal strings support exactly the escapes `\\`, `\"`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, and `\0`; any other escape is a lexical error.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 15 states verbatim: 'They support exactly `\\`, `\"`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, and `\0`. Any other escape is a lexical error.' The positive test's expected 13 bytes (61 5C 62 22 63 0A 64 0D 65 09 66 00 67) are derived by applying that closed list to the source; the negative test uses `\q`, which is outside the list, so rejection plus its LEXICAL category are both spec-determined. The specification names NO code for this error (LANGUAGE_SPEC.md contains no SOLV-LEX-* code anywhere), and TCK.md section 6 forbids promoting an implementation enum entry to normative, so only the protocol family is asserted and diagnosticNormative is false.
normativeQuotes: Normal strings cannot contain an unescaped physical newline. They support exactly \\, \", \n, \r, \t, and \0. Any other escape is a lexical error.

requirements.summary: String interpolation is deferred and a `$` has no interpolation meaning, so `$` and `${...}` inside a normal string are ordinary literal text.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 15 states verbatim: 'String interpolation is deferred. A `$` has no interpolation meaning in the initial implementation.' Because the specification fixes `$` as literal text, the positive observable (the `$`-bearing text emitted unchanged) is determined by the spec, so this is a legitimate assertion rather than a test of deferred behavior: it asserts the specified absence of meaning, not an unspecified feature. The `${value}` shape is included because that is exactly the form interpolation would consume.
normativeQuotes: A $ has no interpolation meaning in the initial implementation.

requirements.summary: Programmers may explicitly write `;`: an explicit semicolon and a newline-inserted semicolon terminate a declaration equivalently under lexical semicolon insertion.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 16 states verbatim: 'Programmers may explicitly write `;`, but normal style uses newlines.' Both declarations therefore introduce their bindings in the same scope and the program is accepted, so the observable is the two values joined by `-`, i.e. the bytes `1-2`. The `..` used to observe them is owned by REQ-0001 and is only the vehicle here (TCK.md section 10's one-obligation preference).
normativeQuotes: Programmers may explicitly write ;, but normal style uses newlines.

requirements.summary: An unterminated raw string is a lexical error at its opening delimiter.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 15 states verbatim: 'An unterminated raw string is a lexical error at its opening delimiter. The diagnostic must show the exact closing delimiter that was expected.' The spec thus determines the rejection AND that it is lexical, so the family is asserted. The required message content is NOT asserted: TCK.md section 7 states human-readable diagnostic wording is not normative unless the specification explicitly says it is, section 15 constrains message content without fixing its text, and TCK.md section 6.1 forbids the TCK choosing an undetermined observable. No code is asserted because the spec names none (no SOLV-LEX-* code exists in the specification).
normativeQuotes: An unterminated raw string is a lexical error at its opening delimiter.

requirements.summary: Normal strings cannot contain an unescaped physical newline.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 15 states verbatim: 'Normal strings cannot contain an unescaped physical newline.' The test breaks a string literal across two physical lines, so rejection plus the lexical category are spec-determined. Only the family is asserted: the spec names no code (no SOLV-LEX-* code exists in LANGUAGE_SPEC.md), and TCK.md section 6 forbids adopting an implementation code. The oracle deliberately requires only that a LEX-family diagnostic is PRESENT rather than that it be the only diagnostic, because an implementation may legitimately also report a follow-on parse diagnostic; requiring a singleton would over-constrain an observable the spec leaves open (TCK.md section 6.1).
normativeQuotes: Normal strings cannot contain an unescaped physical newline.

requirements.summary: Integral division truncates toward zero (sign-symmetrically), as distinct from floor division.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 4 (and section 3) state verbatim: 'Integral division truncates toward zero and division by zero raises a Solvik runtime arithmetic error.' Truncation toward zero is sign-symmetric and differs from floor division only on negative operands, so the oracle asserts all four sign combinations 7/2, -7/2, 7/-2, -7/-2 = 3, -3, -3, 3; floor division would yield -4 for two of them, which is what makes the negative cases pin the rule. `print` appends no separator (section 5), so expected bytes are `3|-3|-3|3`.
normativeQuotes: Integral division truncates toward zero and division by zero raises a Solvik runtime arithmetic error.

requirements.section: 4. Root Type Hierarchy (IEEE 754) / 3. Equality and reference identity
requirements.summary: `Float` and `Double` follow IEEE 754 arithmetic, and floating equality preserves IEEE behavior: NaN is unequal to every value including itself, positive and negative zero are equal, and infinities compare by value.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 4: '`Float` and `Double` follow IEEE 754 arithmetic', and section 3: 'Floating equality preserves IEEE behavior: NaN is unequal to every value including itself, positive and negative zero are equal, and infinities compare by their values.' Expected bytes `false|true|true|true`. NaN and the infinities are produced by 0.0/0.0 and +/-1.0/0.0, which IEEE defines, so the oracle never relies on a floating literal's rendered text. The `nan != nan` case additionally exercises section 3's '`!=` ... negate the corresponding positive operation without evaluating either operand again'. Expected booleans are `true`/`false` per section 4's rendering rule ('`Boolean` renders `true` or `false`').
normativeQuotes: Float and Double follow IEEE 754 arithmetic.
NaN is unequal to every value including itself, positive
and negative zero are equal, and infinities compare by their values.

requirements.section: 3. Equality and reference identity (widened equality comparison)
requirements.summary: `==`/`!=` between numeric operands of different types first widen both to their least common widened numeric type, so `1 == 1L` compares as `Long` and `1.5f == 1.5` compares as `Double`.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 3 states verbatim: '`==`/`!=` between two numeric operands of different types first widen both to their least common widened numeric type (section 4), so `1 == 1L` compares as `Long` and `1.5f == 1.5` compares as `Double`' -- both asserted cases are the specification's own literal examples. `1L` is the `L`-suffixed Long literal of section 1 and `1.5f` the `F`-suffix Float literal ('an `F` suffix selects `Float`'), so the source forms are also spec-derived. Expected bytes `true|true`.
normativeQuotes: so 1 == 1L compares as Long and 1.5f == 1.5 compares as Double.

requirements.summary: For `receiver?.member` the member is evaluated only when the receiver is non-null and the result is the member type made nullable; for `left ?? right` the left operand must be nullable and the result is the common type of non-null `left` and `right`.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 5 states verbatim: 'For `receiver?.member`, the member is evaluated only when the receiver is non-null and the result type is the member type made nullable. For `left ?? right`, `left` must be nullable; the result is the common type of non-null `left` and `right`.' With a null subject: coalescing yields the right operand (`Unknown`), safe access yields null (`true` when compared to null), and the section's own flow-narrowing example prints `Doug`. Expected bytes `Unknown|true|Doug`.
normativeQuotes: For receiver?.member, the member is evaluated only when the receiver is non-null and the result type is the member type made nullable. For left ?? right, left must be nullable; the result is the common type of non-null left and right.

requirements.summary: Flow-sensitive narrowing is required: a non-null test narrows the subject to its non-null type within the branch, so a use requiring the non-null type type-checks inside it.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 5 states 'Flow-sensitive narrowing is required' and annotates the narrowed use as '// name is String here'. The oracle makes narrowing load-bearing rather than cosmetic: `greet` is declared to take a NON-NULL `String`, so `greet(nn)` inside `if (nn != null)` is accepted only if narrowing actually changed the analyzed type from `String?` to `String`. SOL-TCK-0031 uses a `val` and SOL-TCK-0037 a `var` with no intervening write, together covering both binding kinds; SOL-TCK-0032 is the matched negative.
normativeQuotes: Flow-sensitive narrowing is required:
print(name) // name is String here

requirements.summary: Narrowing is permitted only while the value cannot be written or invalidated along the path; a write to a `var` invalidates its prior narrowing.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 5 states verbatim: 'Narrowing is permitted only when the analyzed value cannot be written or invalidated along that control-flow path. A write to a `var` invalidates its prior narrowing.' The test writes `mv = null` between the `mv != null` test and a use that requires non-null, so the program must be rejected; SOL-TCK-0037 is the otherwise-identical control with the write removed, which must be accepted, isolating the rejection to the invalidating write alone. The specification names NO code for this rejection, and TCK.md section 6 forbids promoting an implementation enum entry to normative status, so only the protocol family is asserted.
normativeQuotes: Narrowing is permitted only when the analyzed value cannot be written or invalidated along that control-flow path.
A write to a var invalidates its prior narrowing.

requirements.summary: Types are non-null by default and `null` is assignable only to nullable types; initializing a non-null declaration with `null` is a compile-time error.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 5 states verbatim: 'Types are non-null by default', '`null` is assignable only to nullable types', and gives the annotated example `val bad: String = null // compile error`; the test program is that exact declaration. NO code is asserted: the spec names `SOLV-TYPE-001` for an assignability failure only in two other contexts (section 7 static declaration initializers, section 22.1 exception message arguments) and never binds a code to an ordinary local declaration, so generalizing would have the TCK invent a normative code, which TCK.md section 6 forbids. This is recorded as a specification gap to raise.
normativeQuotes: Types are non-null by default.
val bad: String = null // compile error
null is assignable only to nullable types.

requirements.summary: If `S` is a subtype of `T` then `S` is assignable to `T?` and `S?` to `T?`, but `S?` is not assignable to non-null `T`.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 5 states verbatim: 'If `S` is a subtype of `T`, then `S` is assignable to `T?` and `S?` is assignable to `T?`; `S?` is not assignable to non-null `T`.' With S = T = String, `val m: String = n` where `n: String?` must be rejected. Only the protocol family is asserted, for the same reason recorded on REQ-0456: the specification binds no code to an ordinary assignment/type mismatch and TCK.md section 6 forbids adopting an implementation code.
normativeQuotes: If S is a subtype of T, then S is assignable to T? and S? is assignable to T?; S? is not assignable to non-null T.

requirements.summary: Implicit numeric widening holds for exactly the enumerated relation (Byte->Short->Integer->Long; Byte/Short to Float; Byte/Short/Integer to Double; Float to Double); no other conversion is implicit and no narrowing is implicit.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 4 states the widening relation holds 'for exactly' the enumerated pairs, then 'No other conversion is implicit' and 'No narrowing is implicit', and names two specific non-relations: '`Integer` does not widen to `Float` (the 24-bit `Float` significand cannot hold every `Integer`)' and '`Long` widens to neither `Float` nor `Double`'. SOL-TCK-0035 asserts the `Double`->`Float` narrowing rejection and SOL-TCK-0036 the named `Integer`->`Float` rejection; both are drawn from the enumeration and its explicit exceptions. Only the protocol family is asserted (same reasoning as REQ-0456).
normativeQuotes: No other conversion is implicit. Integer does not widen to Float
and Long widens to neither Float nor Double
No narrowing is implicit.

requirements.section: 4. Root Type Hierarchy (least common widened type)
requirements.summary: Arithmetic, ordering, and equality operands widen to the unique minimal type both can widen or stay to; when two numeric operands have no such common type (for example `Long` and `Float`) the operator is ill-typed.
requirements.oracleNotes: LANGUAGE_SPEC section 4 states verbatim: 'When two numeric operands have no such common type (for example `Long` and `Float`) the operator is ill-typed' -- supplying this exact operand pair as its example. `Long` widens only to `Long` and `Float` only to `Double`, so no unique minimal type admits both and `big + f` must be rejected. The specification states the rule but binds no diagnostic code to it, so only the TYPE family is asserted (TCK.md section 6 forbids promoting an implementation code to normative).
normativeQuotes: the least common widened numeric type of the two operands
When two numeric operands have no such common type (for example Long and Float) the operator is ill-typed.

requirements.summary: Range for-in loops: `...` includes the end, `..<` excludes it ascending, `..>` excludes it descending, reversed or empty ranges iterate zero times, and both bounds are evaluated once before the first iteration
requirements.oracleNotes: SOL-TCK-0039/0040/0041 give one byte-exact sequence per range operator, so an implementation that confuses inclusive with exclusive bounds cannot satisfy all three. SOL-TCK-0042 and SOL-TCK-0045 separate the reversed and empty zero-iteration cases with a counter and a marker prefix respectively, so 'did not start' is distinguishable from 'produced no output'. SOL-TCK-0049 mutates the outer bound variable inside the body and prints two independent observables; re-evaluating the bound each iteration yields a different value from the derived one.
normativeQuotes: The loop variable is an implicitly declared immutable `Integer` binding scoped to the loop body. Both bounds are `Integer` expressions evaluated once before the first iteration.
`...` ascends from the start and includes the end, `..<` ascends from the start and excludes the end, and `..>` descends from the start and excludes the end.
A reversed or empty range performs zero iterations rather than raising an error.

requirements.summary: Three-clause `for` with explicit semicolon separators, an omitted condition treated as true, and `break`/`continue` controlling the enclosing loop
requirements.oracleNotes: SOL-TCK-0043 sums a windowed sequence so the derived total (12) differs from both the no-continue (15) and no-break (10) results. SOL-TCK-0044 omits the condition clause and counts passes, so an implementation reading an omitted condition as false prints 0 instead of the derived 3.
normativeQuotes: `for` uses exactly three clauses: an optional local declaration or assignment, an optional Boolean condition, and an optional assignment. The two separators inside `for (...)` are explicit semicolons. An omitted condition is `true`.
`break` and `continue` are valid only inside a loop.

requirements.summary: `is` type tests narrow the checked value where it is stable, `as` performs a checked cast, and an unsuccessful `as` raises a Solvik runtime type error
requirements.oracleNotes: SOL-TCK-0050 reads a member declared only on the tested subtype inside the guard, which demonstrates narrowing rather than mere truth of the test. SOL-TCK-0051 casts a Cat to Dog; the program is well typed (Dog is a subtype of the static type Any), so the failure must be a run-time fault and is classified as the protocol's cast-failure category from protocol.md section 4.1, with empty stdout. The specification gives no vocabulary for null dereference, so no null-dereference oracle is authored anywhere in this corpus.
normativeQuotes: The compiler must narrow the type where the checked value is stable and no intervening write can invalidate the refinement.

requirements.summary: Declaration lookup is order-independent within a module, and the top-level statements form the body of an implicit main

requirements.summary: break and continue outside any loop are compile-time errors

requirements.summary: `S?` is not assignable to non-null `T`, so a member of `T` is unreachable through a `T?` value without narrowing
requirements.oracleNotes: Family-level only: `find` returns `RegexMatch?` and `value` is declared on `RegexMatch`, but no registry code covers member access on a nullable receiver.
normativeQuotes: `null` is assignable only to nullable types. If `S` is a subtype of `T`, then `S` is assignable to `T?` and `S?` is assignable to `T?`; `S?` is not assignable to non-null `T`.

requirements.summary: Every expression `switch` must contain exactly one `default`, and it must remain last, while a statement `switch` may omit it
requirements.oracleNotes: Exact code from the registry. Covers the missing-`default` clause together with the statement-form permission; the count and ordering clauses stay uncovered for the reason recorded in ORACLE_REVIEW.md.
normativeQuotes: Every expression `switch` must contain exactly one `default`, and it must remain last. `switch` does not gain enum or sealed exhaustiveness; that remains the responsibility of `match`. Requiring `default` makes value production explicit for `Integer`, `String`, and regex dispatch, while a statement `switch` may still omit `default` and do nothing when no label matches.

requirements.summary: `Regex` equality is by exact pattern source text and `RegexMatch` equality is by its immutable snapshot
requirements.oracleNotes: An equal/unequal pair for each of the two table rows.
normativeQuotes: | `Regex` | exact pattern source text |
| `RegexMatch` | immutable snapshot: `value`, `start`, `end`, `groupCount`, and every captured group |

requirements.summary: A block expression has its own lexical scope, its earlier statements execute in source order, and a local declared inside it is visible to later items in that block and nowhere outside it
requirements.oracleNotes: Scope isolation is observable through two block expressions that each declare a local of the same name and each mutate one outer variable: the specification fixes the interleaving of prints and the running total, so the exact stdout is derived rather than observed. The negative half (a block-local name visible outside the block) is SOL-TCK-0140.
normativeQuotes: A **statement block** is a brace-delimited block in statement position; its behavior is unchanged. A **block expression** is a brace-delimited block in expression position. It has its own lexical scope and may contain zero or more statements followed by an optional **tail expression**.
A block expression introduces one lexical scope. Earlier statements execute in source order, and a local declared inside the block is visible to later items in that block and nowhere outside it.

requirements.summary: A value-required block whose normally completing path reaches `}` without a tail expression is the compile-time error SEM_BLOCK_RESULT_REQUIRED, and an empty block, a block ending in a local declaration, and a block ending in an assignment are all invalid in expression position
requirements.oracleNotes: Exact code from the 21.9 registry. All three invalid shapes named by the spec share that one code, so they legitimately share the expectation; the oracle-independence guard deliberately exempts rejection tests because a rejection expectation is a rule, not a derived byte stream.
normativeQuotes: Every normally completing path through a value-required block must reach its tail expression. An empty block, a block ending in a local declaration, and a block ending in an assignment are invalid in expression position and do not acquire an implicit `Unit` result:
| `SEM_BLOCK_RESULT_REQUIRED` | `SOLV-SEM-041` | offending block or case body |

requirements.summary: A path that completes abruptly carries no value and does not participate in result joining; a value-required block whose every path completes abruptly has type Nothing and never evaluates a tail expression
requirements.oracleNotes: Nothing is a type no value inhabits, so an all-abrupt block can never satisfy a value-returning function; the value-returning-function rule is the spec-named SOLV-TYPE-012. This is what separates `Nothing` from a fabricated `Unit`/zero/`null` result, which 21.1 forbids.
normativeQuotes: A value-required block whose every path completes abruptly has type `Nothing` and never evaluates a tail expression.

A path **completes abruptly** when it executes `return`, or a valid enclosing-loop `break` or `continue`, before reaching the construct's result. Abrupt completion carries no value and does not participate in result joining.

requirements.summary: A standalone scope block in statement position remains a statement block, so it contributes no value and its locals stay inside it
requirements.oracleNotes: The block must execute its statements in order and produce nothing; the outer variable it assigns is the only observable, so the oracle is a single value.
normativeQuotes: A standalone scope block remains a statement block, and the existing rule that an unused value-producing non-call expression cannot stand alone still applies.

requirements.summary: Explicit and synthesized semicolons are the same token with the same meaning, token origin is never inspected to decide whether a value exists, and comments and blank lines before `}` do not affect tail selection
requirements.oracleNotes: Four spellings of the same block expression must all yield the same value and type, which the spec states directly; a single concatenated stdout proves the equivalence without asserting anything about formatting.
normativeQuotes: Explicit and synthesized semicolons are the same parser token and have the same language meaning, so token origin is never inspected to decide whether a value exists.
Comments and blank lines before `}` do not affect tail selection, and a terminal assignment is a statement and never a tail expression.

requirements.summary: An expression-position `if` may chain through `else if`, every normally completing branch must produce a tail result, and the condition must be Boolean exactly as for statement `if`
requirements.oracleNotes: The chained form is the spec's own example, driven with one input per arm so each arm's string appears in a fixed position. The non-Boolean half cannot pin a code: the implementation reports SOLV-TYPE-005, which appears zero times in the specification, so the expectation is the bare rejection the spec actually forces.
normativeQuotes: The condition must be `Boolean`, exactly as for statement `if`. An expression `if` must have an `else`; a missing `else` is a dedicated compile-time error and does not also fabricate a branch-type mismatch. Every normally completing branch must produce a tail result, and abrupt branches are excluded from result joining:

requirements.summary: Abrupt branches are excluded from result joining, so an `if` expression whose `else` completes abruptly still produces the value of its normally completing branch
requirements.oracleNotes: Uses the specification's `requireName` example verbatim in shape: the `else` returns from the enclosing function, so only the non-null branch is a result of the `if`. Output is bracketed to make the two distinct arms distinguishable in one stream.

requirements.summary: A `switch` in expression position produces a value from its matched case body, while a statement `switch` may omit `default` and do nothing when no label matches
requirements.oracleNotes: Both halves are observable in one program: the expression form yields a string, and a statement switch whose label does not match contributes nothing to stdout. The missing-`default` rejection for the expression form is already SOL-TCK-0012 under REQ-0204.
normativeQuotes: Every expression `switch` must contain exactly one `default`, and it must remain last. `switch` does not gain enum or sealed exhaustiveness; that remains the responsibility of `match`. Requiring `default` makes value production explicit for `Integer`, `String`, and regex dispatch, while a statement `switch` may still omit `default` and do nothing when no label matches.

requirements.summary: Every normally completing case body, including `default`, must end in a tail expression, so a value-position case body ending in a declaration is SEM_BLOCK_RESULT_REQUIRED
requirements.oracleNotes: The 21.9 primary span for SEM-041 is the offending block or case body, which is why a case body shares the block rule rather than acquiring a separate code.
normativeQuotes: Every normally completing case body, including `default`, must end in a tail expression; statements may precede it.
| `SEM_BLOCK_RESULT_REQUIRED` | `SOLV-SEM-041` | offending block or case body |

requirements.summary: The scrutinee of a `switch` is evaluated exactly once
requirements.oracleNotes: A scrutinee call that prints an observation marker makes exactly-once a byte-exact property: one additional evaluation would duplicate the marker, so the oracle discriminates the claim instead of merely tolerating it.
normativeQuotes: The scrutinee is evaluated exactly once. Case labels are tested in source order, only the first matching body executes, and there is no implicit fallthrough.

requirements.summary: A construct's result type is the nearest common declared supertype to which every normally completing branch result is assignable, with no numeric promotion or widening, so `if (c) { 1 } else { 1L }` has type `Number` and is not assignable to `Integer` or `Long`
requirements.oracleNotes: The acceptance half binds the join to `Number`; the rejection half is what proves the join is not `Long`, which any numeric promotion would produce. The rejection is asserted as a bare rejection: the specification names SOLV-TYPE-001 for a static initializer, not for a local initializer, so no code is spec-mandated at this site.
normativeQuotes: Every value-producing construct uses one shared join algorithm: the result is the nearest common declared supertype to which every normally completing branch result is assignable, including the existing nullability rules. No numeric promotion or widening, structural typing, dynamic typing, implicit conversion, or inferred union type is introduced: a numeric widening is a coercion at a conversion site, never a join rule, so `if (c) { 1 } else { 1L }` has type `Number`, not `Long`.

requirements.summary: If exactly one branch can complete normally, its result type is the construct's result type, and `Unit` participates in the join as any other non-null value type
requirements.oracleNotes: Two different branch types joining to their nearest common supertype is the same rule the join clause states; binding the result to `Any` is the specification's own worked example.
normativeQuotes:
If exactly one branch can complete normally, its
result type is the construct's result type.

`Unit` participates in the join as any other
non-null value type.

requirements.summary: Block, `if`, and `switch` expressions are accepted wherever the grammar accepts an expression, including assignment right-hand sides, call arguments, explicit `return` values, and nested expression constructs
requirements.oracleNotes: Each named context appears once, and the oracle is the concatenation of the values each context must produce.
normativeQuotes: Block, `if`, and `switch` expressions are accepted wherever the grammar accepts an expression, subject to ordinary precedence and any required parentheses, including local initializers, assignment right-hand sides, call arguments, explicit `return` values, operands and nested expression constructs, and `match` branch results:

requirements.summary: A function body does not implicitly return its final expression, so a value-returning function whose body evaluates but does not return is rejected
requirements.oracleNotes: The specification's own `invalid` example is used verbatim. It is rejected, and the value-returning-function reachability rule is named SOLV-TYPE-012, so that code is pinned; the implementation's additional SOLV-SEM-003 has zero occurrences in the specification and is deliberately not asserted.
normativeQuotes: Assignments remain statements and are not usable as tail expressions or nested values, and a function body does not implicitly return its final expression:

whether a `try` statement can
still fall through governs the rule that a value-returning function must return on every path
(`SOLV-TYPE-012`)

requirements.summary: A `match` branch may use a block expression for multiple statements, following the same tail-result, scope, and typing rules as any other block expression
requirements.oracleNotes: The spec's `Ok(value) => { println(...); value }` shape, with `print` instead of `println` so the expected bytes are platform-independent. Both arms are exercised so the marker and both values appear in one deterministic stream.
normativeQuotes:
The block follows the same tail-result, semicolon, scope, abrupt-completion, and typing rules as any
other block expression.

requirements.summary: A local declared inside a block expression is visible nowhere outside it, so referencing it after the block is an unknown-name error
requirements.oracleNotes: Exact code from the reference-resolution rule that names SOLV-RESOL-001 for a name with no visible binding.
normativeQuotes: A block expression introduces one lexical scope. Earlier statements execute in source order, and a local declared inside the block is visible to later items in that block and nowhere outside it.

and if none is visible the
reference is `SOLV-RESOL-001`

requirements.summary: A class that declares `override func hashCode` must also declare `override func equals` in the same class declaration, which is SEM_HASHCODE_WITHOUT_EQUALS
requirements.oracleNotes: The mirror image of the already-covered equals-without-hashCode rule (REQ-0002 / SOLV-TCK-0003). Exact code from the 21.9 registry.
normativeQuotes: A class that declares `override func equals` must also declare `override func hashCode` in the same class declaration, and a class that declares `override func hashCode` must also declare `override func equals`.
| `SEM_HASHCODE_WITHOUT_EQUALS` | `SOLV-SEM-044` | the `hashCode` override declared without `equals` |
